clue: A rare, benign tumor of the adrenal medulla that causes excessive secretion of catecholamines leading to severe hypertension, headaches, palpitations, and intense sweating.
A tumor outside the pituitary gland that produces excessive hormone causing high cortisol levels, severe hypercortisolism, skin hyperpigmentation, high blood pressure, and muscle weakness.
A genetic disorder associated with decreased reaction of body tissues to thyroid hormones.
An extremely rare, autosomal recessive disorder characterized by dark, thick skin, growth retardation, and dysmorphic facial features.
A group of inherited genetic disorders that cause endocrine tumors. Common symptoms include high calcium levels, neck pain, or hormone imbalances.
A highly aggressive central nervous system tumor that often presents with headache, vomiting, seizures, ataxia, and cranial nerve palsies.
A genetic, neuromuscular disorder that causes progressive degeneration resulting in muscle weakness, atrophy, and difficulty with movement, swallowing, and breathing.
An inherited neurodegenerative disorder leading to DNA repair failure. Progressive walking difficulties, balance issues, and dilated blood vessels in eyes/skin are early childhood symptoms.
A rare, progressive, and chronic inflammatory neurological disease, causing severe, drug-resistant epilepsy, cognitive decline, and progressive hemiparesis primarily in children under 15 years.
A polio-like neurological condition causing sudden muscle weakness, loss of reflexes, and limb paralysis due to spinal cord gray matter inflammation requiring immediate hospitalization.
A rare genetic condition combining urinary incontinence, kidney damage, and an inverted facial expression where smiling appears as crying.
A potentially life-threatening infection involving gas-forming bacteria within the bladder wall, occurring in diabetic, elderly females and presenting with abdominal pain, fever, and dysuria.
A condition considered one of the most severe birth defects, causing protruding internal organs, a non-fused pelvis, major spinal abnormalities, a shortened colon, and an imperforate anus.
An uncommon, pouch-like sac that develops along the female urethra, which can cause pelvic pain, frequent urinary tract infections, blood in urine, and incontinence.
A rare, inherited autosomal recessive disorder where an excess production of oxalate combines with calcium, leading to recurrent kidney stones, nephrocalcinosis, and often progressive renal failure.
A rare malignancy that develops in the lower uterine segment or cervix several decades after pregnancy and typically presents as abnormal vaginal bleeding.
An exceptionally rare and aggressive cancer primarily affecting infants and young children, originating in the lungs and pleura, and presenting with cough, shortness of breath, and fever.
An aggressive soft tissue cancer, typically affecting young adults near joints in the limbs and causing slow-growing, painful, deep-seated masses.
A rare tumor of the adrenal gland that causes overproduction of adrenaline and noradrenaline, leading to severely high blood pressure, headaches, palpitations, and excessive sweating.
A unique and aggressive liver tumor that occurs distinctively in young patients without underlying liver disease.
